# FosterStack

Infrastructure worth keeping — and kept patched.

> Maintained continuity for build infrastructure that vendors orphan. Our first
> product, FosterStack Cache, is a self-hosted remote build cache for Gradle and
> Maven — a replacement for the Develocity Build Cache Node, which reaches
> end of life on December 31, 2026.

Gradle Inc. deprecated the free standalone Develocity Build Cache Node: no further
distribution, support, or updates after 2026-12-31. Teams running it on open-source
Gradle, with no Develocity licence, are orphaned on 2027-01-01. FosterStack Cache
speaks Gradle's documented `HttpBuildCache` protocol — acceptance-tested against a
real multi-module Gradle build in CI — and implements the Apache Maven Build Cache
Extension's remote HTTP mode. Same server,
same core.

It is a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), MIT-licensed, distributed as bare
binaries and distroless container images. Every release is keylessly signed with
Sigstore and carries SLSA build provenance, so the exact bytes you deploy are
verifiable against the CI run that produced them.

## Guides on this site

- [Build Cache Node end of life: what happens and your options](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-node-end-of-life/): The free Develocity Build Cache Node will no longer be distributed or supported after December 31, 2026. What stops, what keeps working, your three options.
- [Migrate from Build Cache Node: setup, checklist, checks](https://fosterstack.com/migrate-build-cache-node/): Move from the Develocity Build Cache Node to a self-hosted cache: setup steps, a migration checklist with a real run, and what to check in any replacement.
- [Your Laptop Builds Reuse What CI Already Built](https://fosterstack.com/laptop-builds-reuse-ci-build-cache/): Stop rebuilding on your laptop what CI already built. CI stores results in one shared Gradle or Maven build cache and your laptop restores them. FosterStack Cache.
- [Does a Remote Cache Slow Your Build When It Misses?](https://fosterstack.com/remote-build-cache-miss-cost/): Does asking a remote build cache slow a build when nothing is cached? Seven timed runs on a hosted runner: a miss added about 1 s, a hit saved about 4 s.
- [How Do I Know My Build Cache Hit Rate?](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-hit-rate-how-to-measure/): Two numbers describe a build cache hit rate: the build log and the server counters. Real Gradle and Maven runs show why they differ. FosterStack Cache 0.2.1.
- [Can Someone Poison Our Shared Build Cache?](https://fosterstack.com/can-someone-poison-our-build-cache/): Is a shared build cache safe? Real runs: what the write login can change, what the read-only login refuses, and why isPush false is no lock.
- [What Happens to My Build When the Cache Server Is Down?](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-server-down-what-happens/): Does a Gradle or Maven build fail if the cache server is down? Real 0.2.1 runs, plus what two servers do. Builds finish locally; a dead address cost Gradle 30 s.
- [Does the Build Cache Work With Kotlin and Android Builds?](https://fosterstack.com/kotlin-android-gradle-build-cache/): Does Gradle's remote build cache restore Kotlin and Android tasks? Real runs on FosterStack Cache 0.2.1 show which come from the cache and which rerun.
- [Can Feature Branches Share the Build Cache With Main?](https://fosterstack.com/feature-branches-share-build-cache-with-main/): Do feature-branch builds reuse what main built, and do they change main's cache? Real git branches against FosterStack Cache 0.2.1, with a read-only login.
- [Use a Remote Build Cache in GitHub Actions](https://fosterstack.com/github-actions-remote-build-cache/): Set up a Gradle or Maven remote build cache in GitHub Actions: logins in secrets, a read-only login for pull requests, and what happens when secrets are empty.
- [Is My Build Cache Server Healthy? What to Alert On](https://fosterstack.com/is-the-build-cache-server-healthy-what-to-alert-on/): How to tell a FosterStack Cache server is healthy: what /healthz misses, which counters move when it breaks, what to alert on, and the Prometheus and Grafana setup.
- [Can I Restart the Cache Server While Builds Run?](https://fosterstack.com/restart-build-cache-server-while-builds-run/): What a running Gradle build sees when you restart the cache server, and whether stored results survive a stop or a kill. One warning at most, in our runs.
- [Change the Build Cache Logins Without Breaking CI](https://fosterstack.com/change-build-cache-logins-without-breaking-ci/): In our runs, changing the cache logins did not fail builds. Old-login jobs ran without the cache. Here is an order that keeps the cache working, from a real run.
- [Can Several Projects Share One Build Cache Server?](https://fosterstack.com/several-projects-share-one-build-cache-server/): Many repos, one cache server? In our runs they shared identical work and one size cap, and could read each other's results. Separate servers kept groups apart.
- [Can a Failed or Cancelled Build Poison the Cache?](https://fosterstack.com/failed-or-cancelled-build-bad-results-in-cache/): What a Gradle build leaves in the cache when a task fails, a test fails, you press Ctrl-C or the job is killed. From real runs, including a kill during an upload.
- [Does a Build Cache Entry Contain My Source Code or Secrets?](https://fosterstack.com/does-build-cache-entry-contain-source-code-or-secrets/): We opened every stored entry from real Gradle builds on FosterStack Cache 0.2.1 and searched for fake secrets. What is stored, what is not, and who can read it.
- [Why Did This One Task Miss the Build Cache?](https://fosterstack.com/why-did-this-task-miss-the-build-cache/): One task keeps missing the cache, or a small change reruns the whole build? Diff the cache keys to find the input. Tested on Gradle 9.8.0 and Maven 3.9.9.
- [Build Cache Server Won't Start: Errors and Fixes](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-server-wont-start-errors/): FosterStack Cache exits at start? The log line we got for a busy port, an unwritable data folder (also in a container), a bad setting and a damaged index.
- [Jenkins and CI build cache](https://fosterstack.com/jenkins-ci-build-cache/): Use one shared self-hosted build cache from Jenkins, GitHub Actions or GitLab runners: who should write, in-cluster setup, passwords, and how to check it works.
- [Gradle build cache not working or hit rate low: causes](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-remote-cache-not-working/): Gradle remote build cache not working, hit rate low, or slow after an upgrade? Checks and three causes in order, with real output from FosterStack Cache 0.2.1.
- [Maven remote build cache setup, on/off, and with Gradle](https://fosterstack.com/maven-remote-build-cache-setup/): Set up the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension against a self-hosted remote cache, switch it on and off, and use one server for Gradle and Maven. Real runs on 0.2.1.
- [Gradle build cache on Kubernetes with plain manifests](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-kubernetes/): Run a shared Gradle and Maven build cache on Kubernetes with plain manifests: one replica, update strategy, sizing, security context and in-cluster runners.
- [Security policy](https://fosterstack.com/security/): How to report a security problem in FosterStack Cache or this website, what we aim for on fixes, which version is supported, and the signed files we publish.
- [Verify a release yourself](https://fosterstack.com/verify-a-release/): Verify a FosterStack Cache v0.3.0 release yourself with cosign, gh and jq: image signatures, signed file lists, digests, provenance and the parts list.
- [FIPS 140-3 build cache](https://fosterstack.com/fips-140-3-build-cache/): Run the FIPS build of FosterStack Cache, which uses Go's validated FIPS 140-3 module, and confirm FIPS mode from the startup log and status page. Real output.
- [Reset a build cache](https://fosterstack.com/reset-gradle-build-cache/): There is no purge button. How to empty a self-hosted Gradle and Maven build cache with Docker, Compose, Kubernetes or a plain binary, tested on 0.2.1.
- [Changelog](https://fosterstack.com/changelog/): Release notes for FosterStack Cache v0.1.0, v0.2.1 and v0.2.2, quoted from GitHub, shortened where marked, and a note that no release was published for v0.2.0.
- [Pricing](https://fosterstack.com/pricing/): FosterStack Cache pricing. Free is the full product under MIT. Team $49 a month, Business $199 a month, Compliance $499 a month billed annually. Security patches are never withheld from Free. Paid tiers are described here, not sold.
- [For regulated markets](https://fosterstack.com/regulated/): Evidence and validated crypto for your compliance program: a FIPS build using Go's validated FIPS 140-3 module, with public release evidence.
- [Build cache size limit, eviction and a full disk](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-eviction-size-limit/): How the FosterStack Cache size cap and eviction work, and what a full disk does to uploads, reads and builds. Real runs on 0.2.1, with what to alert on.
- [What to verify in a replacement build cache](https://fosterstack.com/what-to-verify-in-a-replacement-build-cache/): A checklist you can run against any replacement build cache: signed releases, provenance, read-only logins, eviction, metrics, air-gapped use and licence.
- [Is a remote build cache worth it? What we measured](https://fosterstack.com/is-a-remote-build-cache-worth-it/): Measured numbers for a self-hosted remote build cache: Gradle build times with no cache, an empty cache and a filled one, and what Maven restores, each with a public run.
- [FosterStack Cache FAQ: Gradle, Maven, licence, security](https://fosterstack.com/faq/): Short answers about FosterStack Cache: what it is, which Gradle and Maven setups it works with, its licence, how to verify a release, and what happens if it is down.
- [Your first 15 minutes with a self-hosted build cache](https://fosterstack.com/first-15-minutes-build-cache/): A checklist from nothing to your first FROM-CACHE with a self-hosted Gradle build cache, with the commands timed in a real run on release 0.2.2.
- [Let CI write, developers only read: Gradle and Maven cache](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-ci-writes-developers-read/): Let only CI write to the Gradle or Maven build cache and give developers a read-only login the server enforces. Real runs on FosterStack Cache 0.2.1.
- [Gradle remote build cache authentication and 401 errors](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-remote-build-cache-authentication/): Put a password on a self-hosted Gradle build cache, give Gradle the right one, and read the 401, 403, 404, 413 and 429 status codes it returns. Tested on 0.2.1.
- [Maven build cache extension not restoring: the causes](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-extension-not-restoring/): Maven build cache extension builds again instead of restoring from the remote? Causes with real log lines, and whether switching Java 21 to 27 breaks restores.
- [How big a build cache server? CPU, RAM, disk and load](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-server-sizing/): How big a server a self-hosted build cache needs: CPU, RAM and disk, whether a small VM or laptop is enough, and how many builds at once. Real runs on 0.2.1.
- [Air-gapped install](https://fosterstack.com/air-gapped-build-cache-install/): Install a self-hosted Gradle and Maven build cache with no internet: what to download, verify the signature before the transfer, run the binary or container.
- [What changes in v0.3.0](https://fosterstack.com/whats-new-fosterstack-cache-v0-3-0/): What changes for you in FosterStack Cache v0.3.0: what to check before you upgrade.
- [Everything FosterStack does for security](https://fosterstack.com/everything-we-do-for-security/): The security practices that run on FosterStack Cache, one line each, with where to check them.
- [Scanning FosterStack in your compliance pipeline](https://fosterstack.com/scan-fosterstack-cache-image/): How to scan the FosterStack Cache image, and how to apply our published VEX statements in your scanner.
- [Guides](https://fosterstack.com/guides/): Every FosterStack Cache guide, grouped by topic.
- [Roadmap honesty](https://fosterstack.com/roadmap/): What runs today, what is next and how to move the roadmap.
- [How FosterStack Cache is built and signed](https://fosterstack.com/how-we-build/): How a FosterStack Cache release is built, signed and checked, and how to verify it yourself.
- [Production build cache: Docker Compose, nginx and TLS](https://fosterstack.com/build-cache-docker-compose-production/): Run a shared build cache with Docker Compose: a quick start with a password and size limit, then nginx and TLS. The HTTPS setup was run for real on 0.2.1.
- [Build cache behind a corporate proxy: Gradle and Maven](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-corporate-proxy/): Gradle and Maven behind a corporate proxy: the settings, the loopback difference, a refusing proxy, and telling it from a cache error. Gradle 9.8.0, Maven 3.10.0.
- [Enable or Disable the Gradle Build Cache: Flag or Property](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-enable-disable/): Switch the Gradle build cache on or off with --build-cache or org.gradle.caching, and see how it differs from the configuration cache. Tested on a real cache server.
- [Gradle build cache: monorepo, buildSrc and included builds](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-monorepo/): Real runs show what a shared Gradle build cache restores in a four-module monorepo, in buildSrc and in an included build, and what rebuilds. Release 0.2.1.
- [NIST SP 800-204C, 800-204D and SLSA: Our Release Pipeline](https://fosterstack.com/how-our-pipeline-maps-to-nist-and-slsa/): How the new release pipeline maps to NIST SP 800-204C and 800-204D and SLSA.
- [Maven Build Cache Extension in a Multi-Module Project](https://fosterstack.com/maven-build-cache-extension-multi-module/): A real run of the Apache Maven Build Cache Extension on a three-module project with a self-hosted cache: which modules restore, which rebuild, and why.
- [Upgrade, back up and move a build cache server](https://fosterstack.com/upgrade-build-cache-server/): Upgrade FosterStack Cache from 0.1.0 to 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 on the same data volume, back up and restore the volume, and move a Maven cache. All run for real.
- [Skip tests that passed: Gradle and Maven build cache](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-test-task-from-cache/): Do Gradle and Maven skip tests that already passed? Real runs with JUnit against a self-hosted build cache on release 0.2.1, plus a second run on Linux with 0.2.2, including a failing test.
- [What does the build cache store? Gradle and Maven](https://fosterstack.com/what-gradle-stores-in-build-cache/): What a self-hosted build cache holds after real Gradle and Maven builds: which tasks make entries, what each entry weighs, and how to count them. Releases 0.2.1, 0.2.2.
- [Use your Gradle build cache over HTTPS with a private CA](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-remote-build-cache-private-ca-https/): Fix the PKIX path building failed error for a Gradle build cache behind HTTPS with a private CA: trust store settings and a Maven Central trap. Tested on 0.2.1.
- [Reuse Gradle results in Docker CI, even in fresh containers](https://fosterstack.com/gradle-build-cache-docker-ci-fresh-container/): Does a Gradle remote build cache work when each CI build runs in a new container? Real runs in Linux containers on Docker Desktop, with a login. Release 0.2.1.

## Product

- [FosterStack Cache on GitHub](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache): MIT-licensed source, issues, releases.
- [Install guide](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/install.md): supported platforms, which archive to download, systemd unit.
- [One-command Docker deploy](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/docker-deploy.md): includes sizing guidance for CPU, RAM and disk.
- [Deploying on Kubernetes](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/kubernetes.md): plain manifests, no Helm chart yet.

## Setup for your build tool

- [Gradle setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/gradle.md): point `HttpBuildCache` at the server.
- [Maven setup](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/maven.md): Apache Maven Build Cache Extension, remote HTTP mode.
- [Migrate off Build Cache Node](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/migrate-from-bcn.md): the URL is usually the only thing that changes.

## Verification and compliance

- [Verify our images](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/verify-images.md): cosign signature and SLSA provenance, with copy-pasteable commands.
- [Scanning in your compliance pipeline](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/scanning.md): what a scanner sees in a distroless image, and why.
- [Installing on disconnected networks](https://github.com/fosterstack/cache/blob/main/docs/offline-install.md): air-gapped transfer and verification.
- A FIPS build variant (`-fips`) uses Go's CMVP FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic module. Linux only.

## Platform support

- Binaries: `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. From v0.3.0 there is no macOS archive; on a Mac, run the Linux image under Docker Desktop.
- FIPS binaries: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`.
- Container images: multi-arch manifests covering `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.
- Windows is not built and not planned; use WSL2, which is `linux/amd64`.

## Status

The cache core, HTTP surface, eviction, metrics and the signed release pipeline are
shipped and testable today. There is no published schedule for what follows; the roadmap
below says direction, not dates.

Not built:

- Production use beyond the project's own CI.
- A Helm chart. Deploying to Kubernetes today means applying plain manifests.
- The paid tiers. Team ($49/mo: multi-user access control, SSO, per-project
  analytics, email support), Business ($199/mo: adds HA/replication, priority
  support with the CVE-response target), and Compliance ($499/mo billed
  annually: adds the FIPS applicability statement, a monthly
  attestation letter covering every release, questionnaire hours) are described,
  not yet purchasable; the license key that unlocks them is not built.
  Everything in the repository is the free MIT core, including the -fips image
  and all release evidence.
- A CVE patch commitment that can be relied on. Vulnerable dependencies fixed fast — our target is 48 hours from disclosure.

Please do not describe unshipped items as available, and do not attach dates to them.

## Privacy

The server makes no outbound network connections: no telemetry, no phone-home, no
licence check. It runs identically with no route to the internet.

fosterstack.com collects no email addresses, has no signup or waitlist form, sets no
cookies, and runs no analytics. The only personal data FosterStack LLC holds is the
minimum required to bill a paying customer (via Stripe) and voluntary support
correspondence. Do not describe this as "collects no personal data at all" — billing
requires an email address.
